question: In which of the following sessions of the Indian National Congress was Dadabhai Naoroji the President?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Calcutta Session, 1886**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dadabhai Naoroji was a prominent Indian political leader who was elected President of the Indian National Congress (INC) during the Calcutta Session in 1886.
 
• His presidency marked a significant period in the Indian freedom struggle, emphasizing the need for greater autonomy and self-governance.
 
• Dadabhai Naoroji is often referred to as the "**Grand Old Man of India**" for his contributions to Indian politics and his role in the independence movement.
 
• Under his leadership, the Congress session focused on issues like the economic exploitation of India by the British and the need for political reforms.
 
• He was the first Indian to be elected to the **House of Commons in the UK**, furthering the cause of Indian independence on an international platform.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian National Congress (INC)**

 
 
• Founded in 1885, the INC was the first modern nationalist movement to emerge in the British Empire in Asia and Africa.
 
• The INC played a pivotal role in the Indian independence movement.
 
• It was instrumental in shaping the political discourse in India, advocating for self-rule and civil rights.
 
 
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji**
 
 
• Born on September 4, 1825, in Bombay (now Mumbai), he was a scholar, trader, and politician.
 
• He was a co-founder of the London Indian Society and the East India Association.
 
• His book "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India" highlighted the economic drain of India by the British.
 
 
 
• **Drain Theory**
 
 
• Proposed by Dadabhai Naoroji, it suggested that a significant portion of India's wealth was being transferred to Britain, leading to widespread poverty in India.
 
• The theory emphasized the economic exploitation of India under British rule.
 
 
 
• **Congress Sessions**
 
 
• The annual sessions of the INC were significant events where leaders discussed strategies and policies for the independence movement.
 
• These sessions were platforms for addressing key issues such as economic policies, social reforms, and political strategies.
